doc: List the accounts that can make changes in a project (role holders and the agents they own), named the way activity rows name them — for picking whose changes an activity filter includes or excludes. Pass ids to name accounts a saved filter already holds.
Cheap newer-activity check for the task-detail background poll: latest activity id + new_count across the task and its comm child cards.

Read paged activity for one card (chronological) or a project (newest first), with actor names, card titles and card_ref labels resolved; comments include their body inline. Filter by actor / kind / card type / text; ask for facets to get counts per option.

Admin-only: list activity_sink cards under a project, joined with activity_sink_secret (so has_client_secret reflects storage without exposing the encrypted bytes), activity_sink_state (last_activity_id pointer + last_pushed_at + last_error + pending_since from the pump), the email sink's comm channel and its subscription count.

Admin-only: create or update an activity_sink card (id=0 to insert). sink_kind 'msgraph_teams' broadcasts digests into one Teams channel (MS Graph fields + the pgcrypto-encrypted client_secret, optional on update); sink_kind 'email' opens a project comm_channel (channel_id) for personal notification subscriptions, its filters acting as an admin ceiling. Filters / rollup_minutes are written when present, unchanged when omitted.
Delete one of YOUR notification subscriptions (admins may delete anyone's).
List YOUR notification subscriptions (optionally one project) with their sink, project, comm channel and delivery state (last sent, last error, running rollup window).

Create (id=0, under an email sink) or update one of YOUR notification subscriptions: name, event filter, card filter ('@me' = you), rollup_minutes and enabled. You are always the subscriber; the digest is mailed to your person card's email through the sink's comm channel, grouped by task.
List the email activity sinks you can subscribe under — one per project mailbox an admin has opened for notifications, in projects you can see.

Create an agent owned by the calling user (owner 'self', the default) or, for global admins, a workspace agent owned by the System account (owner 'system') — an integration identity that survives staff turnover. Inserts a user_account row (is_agent=true). Agents are NOT assignable through the assignee picker; the parent routes tasks to them via user_card_agent.set. Rejects when the actor is itself an agent.

Delete an agent owned by the calling user (or by any admin): it loses its roles, tokens, sessions and card routings and is no longer listed; its row stays, marked deleted, so its activity, files and imports keep their author. Rejects when the actor is itself an agent.

Vote approve or reject on a status edge of a task — the task moving from one status to another, named by a request (approval_id) or directly (from_status_id → to_status_id) — with an optional reason that shows in the task's comments. A later vote supersedes an earlier one until the task reaches the edge's target, which settles the round. A record only: it moves nothing. An agent's vote is shown with its owner ('claude (for Dana)') but doesn't answer a request that asked the owner. Requires comment rights on the task.

A task's approvals: its current status, its status-flow actions, the live requests (who is asked, by whom, when, and when settled) and every decision (newest first, with reason and whether the task has since moved on). To find the tasks waiting on someone's vote, use card.select_with_attributes with the tree leaf {attr: approval_waiting_on, op: in, values: ['@me' or person ids]} (and with_approvals for each row's tally).
Withdraw an approval request (id from approval.list). Decisions already given stay in the task's history. Requires edit rights on the task.

Ask people to approve or reject one of a task's status actions (from_status_id → to_status_id, a step of its flow, e.g. Review → Done), or change who is asked / the note (with id). Approvals are a record, not a gate: nothing blocks or moves the task. Each person asked must have a login and be able to vote: comment rights on the project's tasks (activity.actors' can_vote). When asking, email: {channel_id} also emails them: a comm thread on the task with the note as its message (note required), linked from the request; they still vote on the task. Requires edit rights on the task (and comm create rights to email).

List a project's areas (Tasks, Conversations, Approvals, Content) with their state — on, off, or unused — starting points and screens; without a project, the whole catalog, including the workspace areas (Sites) and their state. An area that is off is hidden completely.

Switch an area on or off. Off hides everything in it from everyone, refuses changes to it and pauses its automation; on restores it (admin only), turning on the areas it needs and adding a starting point if it never had one. A project area needs project_id; Sites is workspace-wide.
Link an existing file (created via file.create) to a card. Inserts the attachment row + an attachment_create activity in one tx.
Soft-delete an attachment. The file + chunks linger until the CAS reaper sweeps them.

Mint a time-limited, signed URL for an attachment's bytes (mode: download|view|thumb). GET the URL with no auth header — e.g. `curl -o file <url>` — to stream the file straight to disk. The link expires after a few minutes.
List active attachments for a card, newest first.

Mint a time-limited, signed one-shot URL for uploading a file as an attachment on a card. PUT the raw file bytes to the URL with no auth header — e.g. `curl -T ./report.pdf '<url>'` — and the server stores the bytes, creates the file, and attaches it to the card in one step, responding with the attachment row. The link expires after a few minutes; the size cap is config.get's attachment_max_bytes.
Set an attribute value on a card; emits one activity row and one upsert per write.
Admin-only: insert a new attribute_def with optional initial edges, in one tx.
List every attribute_def with the card_types it is bound to via edge.

Add feature bundles to a project: their statuses + flow, screens, filters and starter content are copied in. Re-applying a feature adds only what's missing; a feature whose flow would replace one the project already has is refused. Admin only, like switching an area on (area.set), since it can set an area up.
List the feature bundles (task tracking, conversations, publishing, …) and project presets this install ships. With project_id, also report which features that project has and which it can't take.
Delete one of YOUR calendars; its URLs stop working.
List YOUR calendar feeds: each one's filter, window and secret URLs (with when and by which app each was last fetched).

Create (id omitted) or update one of YOUR calendar feeds: title, card filter ('@me' = you; empty = every task you can see) and window (past_days / future_days, 0–3650, defaults 30 / 365). Tasks with a due date in the window become all-day events.

Add a secret URL to one of YOUR calendars, with a comment saying where it's used. Returns the token once: subscribe to /api/v1/calendar/<token>.ics. Calendar services fetch it from their own servers, so task titles go to them.
Revoke a calendar URL; it stops working at once.
Change a calendar URL's comment.
Soft-delete a card; the row is hidden from default selects but kept for activity history.

Insert a new card with the given card_type, optional structural parent (parent_card_id), and initial title plus attributes. To create a TASK as a subtask of another task, pass parent_task (the existing parent task's id) — that sets the parent/child link the task UI shows, distinct from parent_card_id which is the enclosing project.

Fold one or more duplicate cards of the same card_type into a survivor: repoint every card_ref / card_ref[] reference to the survivor and soft-delete the losers. For deduplicating value cards (milestones / components / tags). People are refused (use_person_merge: person.merge keeps their logins and private cards apart), and so is a state a flow uses (value_referenced_by_flow) or merging cards into a state you couldn't move them into (flow_role_required).
Re-parent a card under a different parent of a compatible card_type.
Lightweight typeahead read for ref:* picker dropdowns. Returns (id, title) of cards in card_type_name that match query (substring) and/or ids.
List cards filtered by optional parent and card_type; soft-deleted rows are excluded.
Select cards plus their full attribute set in one round-trip; supports filters and ordering for grids and kanbans.
Set the structural phase column on a value-card (triage|active|terminal); emits an activity row recording the change.
Undo a previous soft-delete by clearing deleted_at on the card.
List every card_type row known to the server (built-in types are seeded via migration).

Given a list of cas_blob addresses, return the subset NOT currently stored. Used by the client as an upload pre-flight: bytes for the missing addresses are POSTed to /api/v1/cas/chunk; everything else is skipped.

Move a thread (comm card) onto a task in the same project, or detach it back into its project as a thread on its own (task_id 0); with new_task_title and no task_id, make a task with that title and attach the thread to it, in one go. Keeps both tasks' comms lists in step. Files stay where they are: a thread keeps the files that came by email (move one onto the task with comm.attachment_to_task). Refused while Tasks is switched off (area_off). Authz: card.update on comm (the dispatcher) plus card.update on task in the project, and card.create on task to make one (checked in SQL).

Add to task: move a file that came by email (it lives on the thread) onto the thread's task, so it shows in the task's attachments; the messages that carried it keep their link. When the task already holds the same bytes, the messages link that file and the thread's copy goes — the task never has a file twice. Refused for a thread not on a task (not_on_task) and while Tasks is switched off (area_off). Authz: card.update on comm (the dispatcher) plus card.update on task in the project (checked in SQL).

Create a comm card under a task (worker / manager / admin, scoped to the task's project). Generates a 10-char alphanumeric thread_id, sets channel_ref + comm_status (the project's comm flow default_create_status_id), appends the new comm to the task's comms attribute, and (when initial_message is provided) creates an outbound reply_body row (delivery_status='pending', queued for SMTP) — which requires recipient_person_ids.

Return every comm card under the task, hydrated with its replies (reply_body cards listed in the comm's replies attribute) — or, with comm_id, that one comm (a thread on its own sits directly in its project). Read-side affordance for the task detail and thread screens; any authenticated user may call.

Set the per-thread `acked` flag on a comm card (true = handled, default; false = re-open). A received inbound reply clears it automatically. Authz: worker / manager / admin (matches the manager grant on comm).
Replace the comm_recipients participant list on a comm card. Pass an empty array to clear. Each id must reference a person card. Authz: worker / manager / admin (matches the manager grant on comm).

Cheap count of newly received comms (inbound reply_body cards) across every project the caller can see, with create-activity id > since_activity_id. Drives the header notification bell; any authenticated user may call.

Admin-only: list comm_channel cards configured under a project, joined with their comm_secret row so has_imap_password / has_smtp_password indicate which passwords have been set without exposing the encrypted bytes.

Admin-only: create or update a comm_channel card (id=0 to insert) plus its paired comm_secret row holding pgcrypto-encrypted IMAP + SMTP passwords. Password fields are optional on update; omitted passwords leave the stored value unchanged.
Admin-only: paginated read of comm_log rows for a project, optionally filtered by kind and a since timestamp (defaults to last 24h).

Admin: add an inbound route to a mail account — a POST URL for a provider (raw: Cloudflare Email Worker / SES via Lambda / scripts; mailgun: needs the webhook signing key; postmark: turn on 'include raw email') or an address for kitp's SMTP listener. Returns the secret token once.
Admin: remove an inbound route; its URL or address stops working at once.
Admin: a mail account's inbound routes — POST URLs and SMTP addresses — with their comment, filters, and last message / refusal. Filter the Comm log by route_id to see a route's traffic.
Admin: change an inbound route's comment, filters or Mailgun signing key.
Post a comment on a card; writes one comment_body row and one activity row of kind=comment.
Edit the body of an existing comment. Updates the linked comment_body row in place and inserts a new activity row of kind='comment_edit' for the audit trail. Only the original author may edit.
Return server-driven configuration values the client needs (e.g. attachment size caps).
Echo the input back unchanged; used to smoke-test the dispatcher.
Admin-only: unbind an attribute_def from a card_type. Refuses with usage_count if any attribute_value rows reference it.
Admin-only: bind an existing attribute_def to a card_type. Idempotent (re-binding is a no-op).
Insert a logical file (filename + size + mime + chunk list) from a chunk list previously uploaded via POST /api/v1/cas/chunk.
Admin-only: delete one flow row. Refuses with code='flow_disallowed' and a {blockers[], count} payload when any flow_step row still references the flow; admins must clear steps first.
List flow rows, optionally filtered by scope_card_id (project) and / or attribute_def_id. Available to any authenticated user.

Admin-only: dry-run preview for flow.delete. Returns step count, affected-task counts (total + phase breakdown), and up to 5 sample step labels so the admin dialog can show consequences before the destructive call (V16).
Admin-only: upsert one flow row (per-project state machine on an attribute_def). id=0 inserts; id>0 updates by id.
Admin-only: delete one flow_step row by id.
List flow_step rows for one flow, joined to the optional requires_role name. Sorted by sort_order then label.

Read-side affordance API: return every flow_step the given card may currently fire — one row per (flow, attribute_def, from_card_id=card's value) match — pre-joined with from/to titles + phases, optional requires_role name, and a per-actor allowed bit. Gate 5's attribute.update rejection envelope reuses the same query.
Admin-only: upsert one flow_step row. id=0 inserts; id>0 updates by id. Without id, the (flow_id, from_card_id, to_card_id, label) unique key rejects duplicates.
Compose per-screen help: layout primer + plain-English description of the default filter.
Return the authored markdown for a named help topic (admin.screens, layout.kanban, ...).
Remove a link from its task (id from link.list). Requires edit rights on the task. Not sticky: linking the same URL again adds it back.
List the links on a task (oldest first): url, title, kind / state slugs, when it was added and last changed, and who added it.

Link a URL — a code change (Gerrit CL, pull request), an issue, any page — to a task, or update an existing link. Idempotent: the URL is the link's identity on the task, so linking it again PATCHes the same link (title / kind / state) instead of adding a duplicate, and re-sending unchanged values writes nothing. kind / state are short slugs (e.g. kind 'gerrit', state 'open' | 'reviewed' | 'approved' | 'merged' | 'abandoned'). Requires edit rights on the task.

Admin: the mail intake listener's state — SMTP settings and certificate, trusted proxies, rate limits, sources currently throttled and the last connection-level refusals (kept in memory; reset on restart).
Delete one of YOUR personal screens and its views.
List YOUR personal screens (Mine in the left navigation): name, layout, what they list, base filter, order and default view.

Create (id omitted) or update one of YOUR personal screens: a list or grid of tasks or threads across every project you can see, narrowed by a base filter (a project leaf limits it to some projects). Only you see it. Save views on it with card.insert {card_type_name: filter, parent_card_id: <screen>} — they are yours too.
List the portals a page is published to: when, by whom, whether that copy is current, and its path in the portal's active build.

Create a new person card with the given title, optional email, and tier ('contact' | 'assignee' | 'user'). When tier='user' a user_account row is also created (oidc_sub NULL — attached on first sign-in) and linked via user_account_person. Admin-only.

Grant a login (user_account) to an EXISTING person card — promote an assignee/contact to a user. The email is required and is the one they will sign in with; the person card's email attribute is never copied (any worker can edit it). Idempotent: a person whose login has that email returns it; a login with another email is already_linked. Admin-only.

Merge duplicate person cards into one survivor: repoint every assignee / originator / comm_recipients reference to the survivor, move a sole login (user_account) to the survivor, backfill the survivor's blank email from a loser, and soft-delete the losers. Rejects with 'merge_login_conflict' when more than one of the people has a login (resolve duplicate user accounts first — merging logins/sessions/tokens is out of scope). Admin-only.

Find a person card by case-insensitive email match, or create a new global person card with the supplied display name + email + kind. Used by the comm recipient picker (kind='contact') so typing a fresh email materialises a contact card in one round trip. Authz: worker / manager / admin.
List portals with their root page, host, theme, whether they show inside kitp, the statuses that publish to them, and their build state (pages, built at, warnings, pending rebuild, last error).
Queue a portal for rebuilding (builds otherwise follow publication changes). Admin only.

List the pages a portal can use as its root: live pages in projects that aren't templates, each labelled with its project and parent pages ('Docs › Home › Guide'). Feeds the Portals screen's root-page picker. Admin only.

Create or update a portal (a published site): its title, root page, public host name, whether it is served publicly or only as a signed-in preview, whether it shows inside kitp, and its theme. Which pages it shows is set on statuses (publishes_to). Admin only.

Search the registered handler catalogue. Defaults to handlers the caller can actually invoke; pass include_unavailable=true to see every match regardless of role. Combine with {all:true} or {query, endpoint, action} filters.

Create a project from a preset (bundle.list presets) and/or a list of feature bundles, instead of copying a template. Each feature's statuses + flow, screens, filters and starter content are copied in, in order.

Create a fresh project by graph-copying a template project's value cards, screens, filters, flows, and flow_steps with ID remapping. Tasks, comments, activity, and per-user state are not copied (FLOW_AND_SCREEN_KERNEL §Project templates / Gate 10).

Author an outbound reply on a comm. Inserts a reply_body card with delivery_status='pending', inherits reply_from from the comm's channel from_address attribute, and appends the new id to the comm's replies attribute. The SMTP sender (Gate 5) picks up pending rows on its next tick. worker / manager / admin may author.
List every role and its granted (card_type, process) pairs. The admin UI uses this to populate the role picker.
Admin-only: delete one role_mapping row by claim_value.
List every role_mapping row (claim value -> role).
Admin-only: upsert one role_mapping row.
Apply a tag card to a target card; mutually-exclusive sibling tags at the same root are removed atomically.
Remove a tag card from a target card.

Move a task (and optionally its sub-tree) to a DIFFERENT project, clearing per-project classification so the user re-classifies in the destination. This is a cross-project move, NOT subtask nesting: source and destination must be different projects (a same-project call returns same_project). To nest one task under another as a subtask, set the child's parent_task attribute via attribute.update, or pass parent_task to card.insert at create time.
Permanently delete a task (and its comms / reply_bodies / attachments / activity). Refuses when live sub-tasks or flow references exist. UI must gate this behind a strong confirm.
Read one file of a built-in theme (read-only), e.g. to start a theme's own page.html or custom.css from it. Admin only.
List the built-in themes (Side menu, Top menu, Newspaper, …) with their files. A theme card starts from one of them. Admin only.
Remove one of a theme's files, so its base theme's file of that name (if any) applies again. Rebuilds the portals using the theme. Admin only.
Read one of a theme's own files. Admin only.

Add or replace one of a theme's files: a template (page.html, or a file of {{define}} blocks), custom.css, theme.json, logo.* / favicon.*, a font or an image. A template is checked by rendering a sample site with it. Rebuilds the portals using the theme. Admin only.
List the themes: settings, the files each adds to or overrides in its base, and the portals using it. Admin only.
Create or update a theme: its name, built-in base theme, navigation mode (full, section, collapsible), accent colour and footer. Rebuilds the portals using it. Admin only.
List every user_account row with role assignments and resolved project titles for scoped grants. Used by the admin UI.

Let a login revoked by user.revoke_login sign in again — the Users screen's "Allow sign-in again" — and link it back to the person it was, when that person is live and has no other login. Its roles, sessions and tokens stay gone; grant roles again with user_role.set. not_revoked when the login isn't revoked, or a later login already took over its identity.

Take a person's login away — what the People screen's Remove and "no longer a user" do. The account and its agents lose every role, session and token, and its person link; the login is marked revoked (login_revoked_at) and keeps its sign-in identity (oidc_sub, email), so a sign-in by that identity — or by another with the same verified email — is refused until an admin gives them a login again (person.grant_account lifts it for that email). The row stays, so its activity keeps its author. Refused for the System user, an agent (use agent.delete) and your own login.
List every user_account row sorted by display_name.

Update user_account.display_name for one user_account row. The /auth/me probe reads display_name straight from this column, so this is what powers the shell's signed-in user chip — renaming the linked person card (attribute.update on title) does NOT propagate here. Admin-only; no-op (ok=true) when the value already matches.

Delete the user_account_person link between a user_account row and a person card. The user_account row itself stays — they can still sign in, they just no longer correspond to an assignable person card (demotes 'user' tier to 'login-only'). Idempotent: deleting an absent link succeeds with deleted=false.
Remove the calling user's routing for one card — or, called by an agent, the routing that sends the card to it. Idempotent.
List the calling user's routings, optionally scoped to one parent (e.g. a project).
Route a card to one of the calling user's agents. Upsert keyed on (actor, card). The agent_user_id must be an agent owned by the calling user.
Upsert the calling user's personal sort_order for one card. Used by the inbox drag-drop reorder; per-user ordering is independent of the global sort_order attribute.
List role grants held by one user. Anyone authenticated may query themselves; the parent of an agent may query that agent; admins may query anyone.
Revoke a role from a user (with matching scope). Admin-only EXCEPT when the target is an agent — then the agent's parent_user_id may also revoke.

Grant a role to a user, optionally scoped to a project. Admin-only EXCEPT when the target is an agent — then the agent's parent_user_id may also grant it. Whoever grants, an agent only gets a role its owner holds or ranks above (viewer < commenter < worker < manager < admin), at that scope or workspace-wide. Coalesces N inputs into one upsert statement.

Mint an opaque bearer token bound to user_id. The plaintext value is returned ONCE in the response — store it immediately. scope 'links' mints a narrow token that works ONLY on the forge link hook (POST /api/v1/links), for a code forge; omit it for a full-access (MCP) token. Authz: your own token, one for an agent you own, or (global admin) one for a workspace agent owned by System — never one for another human or their agent.
List every token bound to user_id (label + timestamps; the secret value is never returned). Authz: the user themselves, their owner (for an agent), or a global admin.
Revoke one token by (user_id, label). Idempotent. Authz: the user themselves, their owner (for an agent), or a global admin.

What is on one of YOUR watch lists, in its order: each task or thread with its title, project and status. To filter a screen instead, use the card filter leaf {attr: watch_list, op: in, values: ['@me']} (any of your lists) or list ids.
Move an item on one of YOUR watch lists: give it a sort_order between its new neighbours' (lower first).
Put a task or thread you can see on one of YOUR watch lists (it goes to the top), or take it off (on=false).
Delete one of YOUR watch lists; the tasks and threads on it are untouched.

List YOUR watch lists (bookmark lists of tasks and threads): name, symbol, description and how many items each holds; with card_id, whether that card is on each. Your first call makes your Stars (★) list.
Create (id omitted) or update one of YOUR watch lists: name (1–60 characters), symbol (an emoji or a character; default ★) and description.
